answer: An identity counts only when three sponsors from separate subtrees each lock 120 units behind it for a 12-epoch voyage. A sponsor key backs one identity at a time; the registry rejects a second registration, so backing stays unpoolable. Slashing requires a public proof: an identity signing two answers in one epoch, or a work-sample hash filed by two identities. An honest agent gathers three sponsors once; 1,000 fakes need 3,000 keys and 360,000 units locked. Slashes pay out on the settlement tide, once the proof posts; maturity counts checkpoints from the quartz timestamp at registration.
